name: Investor Residence Card (ANDI)

requirements.blocker_text: The National Investment Development Agency (ANDI) manages the investor residence card. Applicants must create an enterprise or acquire a stake in an Algerian company, submit a feasibility study and business plan, and secure ANDI approval. Reported foreign-ownership limits (a 51/49 rule, Algerian majority ownership) apply in most sectors, per the source reviewed. Processing runs 2-4 months, with administrative costs estimated at EUR 300-800.
requirements.fix_path: Establish or take a stake in an Algerian company, submit the required feasibility study and business plan to ANDI, and obtain approval.

sources.title: Openshores (private immigration-guide site) -- ANDI investor residence card requirements, reported 51/49 foreign-ownership rule, processing time and cost

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Algeria). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to a private immigration-guide blog, tier 4; ANDI's own government page was not independently fetched in this build (Algeria's .gov.dz domains returned SSL/certificate errors on every direct fetch attempt made across this country's build -- a systematic, disclosed access gap). GENUINE, DISCLOSED CAVEAT: the reported 51/49 foreign-ownership cap ('in most sectors' per the source) is a well-known historical feature of Algerian investment law, but this build could not independently confirm whether it still applies as broadly as stated or has been narrowed by more recent reforms -- disclosed as reported-but-not-independently-verified rather than treated as settled current policy. Permit duration itself was not stated by the source and is left unconfirmed rather than guessed.
